assumptions: A single adult ordinary first-offense infraction, without prior-conviction enhancements.
No construction, maintenance, safety-enhancement or other enhanced-penalty zone.
No commercial-vehicle, over-100-mph or other special offense or enhancement.
The selected code, subsection and speed band match the citation; this tool does not decide guilt.
Posted schedule rows or explicitly labeled calculated local references, not a court case lookup, payment demand or traffic-school eligibility decision.
Do not add these references across multiple charges: rounding can apply to the aggregate base, and case-specific charges, reductions and court discretion are not modeled.
unknowns: Your actual court balance and deadline.
Additional case charges, adjustments, reductions or required appearance.
Court permission for traffic school and the separate court traffic-school charge.
School tuition and any insurance effect.

codes.label: Exceeding the 65 mph maximum speed limit
notes: This subsection concerns the 65 mph maximum. Confirm the exact subsection on the citation.
Driving over 100 mph is a different offense and is outside this lookup.

codes.label: Unsafe speed for prevailing conditions
notes: A posted-limit speed difference alone does not determine whether driving was safe for conditions.
If the citation cannot be matched to one of these schedule bands, ask the court; no zero-or-below-limit price is inferred.

codes.label: Red signal: vehicular responsibilities
notes: Confirm subsection (a). The schedule has a separate lower-priced subsection (b) row; this lookup never substitutes it.

codes.label: Holding and operating a handheld wireless telephone or electronic communications device while driving
notes: Zero points is the ordinary first-offense schedule entry, not a statement that every device violation is point-free.
A qualifying repeat conviction within 36 months can carry a point under Vehicle Code 12810.3. Repeat fines and eligibility are outside this lookup.

codes.label: Failure to stop at a stop sign
notes: Confirm subsection (a). Subsection (b) concerns a railroad grade crossing and is not substituted.
Only Santa Barbara has a reviewed ordinary stop-sign amount here. Construction, maintenance and other enhanced-zone cases are excluded; the schedule lists those separately.
One point is the ordinary schedule entry, not a determination about your driving record or traffic-school eligibility.
